A useful post can be a few paragraphs and a clear example. Markdown keeps the formatting close to the writing, so you can edit everything in your repository.

## Give the page some structure

Use second-level headings for the main sections of a post. The default template builds a table of contents from your headings, helping readers find the part they need.

Keep paragraphs focused on one idea. Use **bold text** for a short emphasis and `inline code` for file names, commands or settings.

## Show the steps

1. Describe what the reader is trying to do.
2. Show a small example they can follow.
3. Explain what they should see when it works.

For notes that don't have an order, use a list:

- Name the files the reader needs to change.
- Include the expected result.
- Link to more detail when it helps.

## Include an example

Fenced code blocks keep examples readable:

```json
{
  "name": "Your company",
  "blog": {
    "title": "From the team"
  }
}
```

> Write the explanation you would want to find when you are trying this for the first time.

## Keep the next step clear

Finish with something the reader can do. For this site, start by editing `blog.json`, then replace these sample posts with your own.

The [Notra Sites documentation](https://usenotra.com/docs/sites) covers the configuration and components available when you need more than Markdown.
